intro: Chemical engineers solve complex process problems and evaluate systems, skills used across materials, energy and research. The closest of the 25 careers below is Materials Scientists, with a 94% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $117,790, which is 6% less than the $125,040 chemical engineers earn.
why_it_works: Designing a chemical process means modeling reactions, scaling them safely and fixing bottlenecks in a running plant. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 4 out of 5 for this job, and judgment and systems analysis at 3.88. Materials science, biofuels and water resources use the same expertise. Most matches need no new degree. The gaps are equipment maintenance and programming.
tips: Biofuels product development management is an 85% match with a median of $171,270 for its broader group.
Database Architects earn $139,500, which is 12% more, if you enjoy data and modeling.
Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470, or 18% more, and value quantitative precision.

faq.q: What jobs can former chemical engineers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Materials Scientists (94%), biofuels product development managers (85%) and Water Resource Specialists (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Geoscientists are 70% matched and earn $101,920, which is 18% less than the $125,040 chemical engineer median.

faq.q: Which careers for chemical engineers pay more?
faq.a: 9 of the 25 matches pay more. Physicists earn $172,250 (38% more), Medical Dosimetrists $147,470 (18% more) and Database Architects $139,500 (12% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Physics usually requires a graduate degree, while database and dosimetry work need targeted training.

faq.q: Do chemical engineers need another degree?
faq.a: Usually not. 21 of the 25 matches need no more education than chemical engineers already have, including 9 of the top 10, while 4 usually need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 62% of workers in the closest match.

faq.q: What skills should chemical engineers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment maintenance, programming, repairing and service orientation. Systems evaluation already rates 3.88 out of 5 for chemical engineers in O*NET, so software and hands-on equipment skills are the main steps for most moves.
